descriptions.text:
This course introduces students to linguistic fieldwork and language documentation. Students are trained to carry out linguistic fieldwork by working with a native speaker of an unfamiliar or under-described non-European language. The aim is to collect and analyse sufficient field data to be able to write a basic grammar sketch of the language, and to learn to identify the practical, ethical and theoretical issues that are involved in language documentation.

Data are collected through interviews with a language consultant by using various elicitation and grammar gathering techniques. These sessions will be recorded and the recordings will be made available to the students. Students are also expected to take notes of the data collection during class.
The data collected during the fieldwork sessions will be analysed by applying theoretical knowledge of linguistics on primary data. For this reason, a basic knowledge and understanding of articulatory phonetics, phonology, morphology and syntax is required.
The course takes place twice a week: one class is dedicated to the data collection with the native speaker, and the other is devoted to the discussion and the analysis of the collected data. The data collection sessions will be led by a different group of students each week. The session leaders share their preparation beforehand with the students and the teacher. All students take their own notes and build their own database. 
In the first block, the discussion sessions will be focused on plenary discussion of the data and possible analyses, as well as data collection techniques and ideas for future data collection. In the second block, discussion sessions will focus on language documentation, the differences (and similarities) between language description and language documentation, and the theoretical, practical and ethical aspects of conducting linguistic fieldwork and language documentation.
Weekly homework consists of processing and analysing the newly collected data, as well as assigned readings. The book to be used is:
Bowern, Claire. 2015. Linguistic fieldwork: A practical guide. Palgrave Macmillan.

We will use chapters of the following textbook as background literature during the course. The book is available in the library.

Bowern, Claire. 2015. Linguistic Fieldwork: A practical guide. Palgrave Macmillan.

### Assessment

* Mid-term paper: phonology sketch
* Documentation project proposal
* Final paper: grammar sketch (in groups)
* Elicitation leaders: all students need to lead (prepare, conduct) at least one of the data collection sessions. If you fail to do so, you may not be allowed to complete the course.

### Weighing

Mid-term paper: 20%
Documentation project proposal: 30%
Final paper: 50%

The final mark for the course is established by determining the weighted average. To pass the course, the weighted average of the partial grades must be 5.5 or higher, *and* the final paper and documentation project proposal should have a passing grade.

Enrolment through MyStudyMap (button in upper right corner) is mandatory. General information about course and exam enrolment is available on the website https://www.student.universiteitleiden.nl/en/your-study-programme/courses-and-exams/enrolment/leiden-university

None, but it is advised to have passed Speech Sounds of the World/Klanken van de Wereld.

Students from outside the BA Linguistics are welcome to join too.

If MyStudymap indicates the course is full, please contact the education coordinator ([stuco-ba-linguistics@hum.leidenuniv.nl](mailto:stuco-ba-linguistics@hum.leidenuniv.nl "mailto:stuco-ba-linguistics@hum.leidenuniv.nl")) about admission possibilities. If a larger room cannot be found, priority will be given to students from the BA Linguistics.

For questions about the content of the course, contact the lecturer(s) (listed in the right information bar).  For questions about enrolment, admission, etc., contact the Education Administration Office:  osz-oa-reuvensplaats@hum.leidenuniv.nl
The timetables are available through My Timetable (see the button in the upper right corner).

### Resit

Students can resit the final paper and the documentation project proposal. There is no resit opportunity for the mid-term paper.

### Review and feedback

Students will be provided with feedback on their papers, and general feedback on the mid-term paper will be discussed in class. Students can make an appointment with the teacher for further discussion of feedback if necessary.

descriptions.value: Acquiring knowledge by systematically and methodically inquiring into a situation or concept, making use of methods appropriate to the academic field or discipline.
Kennis verwerven door het systematisch en methodisch bevragen van een situatie of concept waarbij gebruik gemaakt wordt van methoden die passen bij het vakgebied of de discipline.
Analysing situations or information and deciding what is of major and lesser importance. Seeing interrelationships and getting to the core of the matter.
Ontleden van situaties of een hoeveelheid informatie in hoofd- en bijzaken. Zien van onderlinge verbanden en doordringen tot de kern.
Formulating new concepts, conceptual frameworks or models based on complex information and issues.
Formuleren van nieuwe concepten, denkkaders of modellen op basis van complexe informatie en vraagstukken.
Achieving a result by effectively and systematically utilising and overseeing activities, time and resources.
Een resultaat bereiken door het effectief en planmatig inzetten en overzien van activiteiten, tijd en middelen.
Using digital technology, methods, sources or databases to achieve results.
Gebruiken van digitale technologie, methoden, bronnen of databases om resultaten te behalen.
Contributing to a joint result with other people or groups, even when this is not in your own personal interest.
Bijdragen aan een gezamenlijk resultaat met andere personen of groepen, ook wanneer dit niet van direct persoonlijk belang is.
Making ideas and information clear to others through spoken words, using comprehensible language and checking that the message has been understood.
Ideeën en informatie in begrijpelijke gesproken taal aan anderen duidelijk maken en nagaan of de boodschap begrepen is.
Setting out ideas and information clearly in writing, taking account of the relevant target group and in such a way that the message is received and understood.
Ideeën en informatie helder op schrift stellen, rekening houdend met de doelgroep, en zodanig dat de boodschap overkomt en wordt begrepen.
Conveying ideas and information clearly to an audience, taking account of the target group and using appropriate supporting materials and platforms.
Ideeën en informatie op heldere wijze overbrengen aan een publiek, rekening houdend met de doelgroep. Hierbij worden passende ondersteunende materialen en platformen gebruikt.

Critically evaluating own and others’ behaviour, viewpoints or methods, and being open to evaluation by others. Being able to learn from these evaluations by changing own behaviour, viewpoints or methods.

Het kritisch evalueren van (eigen) gedrag, standpunten of methoden en open staan voor evaluatie door anderen. Het vermogen om te leren van deze evaluaties door wijziging van het eigen gedrag, standpunten of methoden.
Self-directing own process of absorbing and applying new knowledge and information.
Zelf sturing geven aan het eigen proces van nieuwe kennis en informatie opnemen en toepassen.
The ability to continue performing effectively in changing and challenging circumstances; to cope with setbacks and recover from them.
Het vermogen om effectief te blijven functioneren in veranderende, uitdagende omstandigheden. Om kunnen gaan met en herstellen van tegenslag.
Being well-informed about societal, political and discipline-related developments and being aware of own role and influence within these developments.
Goed geïnformeerd zijn over de maatschappelijke, politieke en vakinhoudelijke ontwikkelingen en zich bewust zijn van de eigen rol en invloed binnen deze ontwikkelingen.
